paper_metadata.title: Microstructure and mechanical properties of ZrBe alloys processed by hot rolling

evidence.quote: In the present study, the effects of Be content on the microstructure and mechanical properties of hot rolled ZrBe binary alloys were investigated.

parameters.deformation: 65% total thickness reduction (multi-pass to 5 mm plate)

evidence.quote: the ingots were heated from room temperature to 850 °C using a heating velocity of 10 °C/min. then holding for 30 min Subsequently, the heated ingots were multi-pass rolled into plate specimens with a thickness of 5 mm. The total deformation of the rolled samples was 65%.
Following rolling, the specimens were water-quenched.

mechanisms.name: solid solution of Be in Zr matrix limited by low solubility

evidence.quote: Otherwise, the increase in fB can be attributed to the addition of Be element. Low solid solubility of Be in Zr matrix causes the increase in Be 2Zr particles content in the studied alloys.

mechanisms.name: beta phase stabilization by Be lowering alpha-to-beta transition temperature

evidence.quote: In Zr alloys, Be being a β phase stabilizer decreases α phase to β phase transition temperature. Although the studied alloys were rolled at the same temperature, the lower phase transition temperature will induce higher β phase content during the rolling process.

mechanisms.name: martensitic transformation of beta phase during quenching

evidence.quote: β phase is rapidly converted into α' martensite phase during the quenching process

mechanisms.name: Hall-Petch strengthening by alpha prime lath refinement

evidence.quote: By applying the Hall-Petch formula (i.e., s¼s0 þkd/C0 0.5, where s represents the yield strength of the hot-rolled ZrBe alloys and d is the lath width of α' martensite), the s0.2 of the ZrBe alloy increases with decreasing the width of α' martensite.

According to Orowan mechanism [27], the force needed to overcome the barrier by a dislocation significantly increases with the increased resistance. Due to the interaction between the compound particles and dislocations, the strength of the alloys can be improved significantly.

mechanisms.name: grain-boundary stress concentration at segregated Be2Zr particles

evidence.quote: due to the segregation of Be2Zr particles at prior- β grain boundaries, the stress distribution during the loading process was not uniform [29,30]. Stress concentration occurred near the grain boundaries led to the generation of cracks during further deformation.
